title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 2, Fugue 16 in G minor

character.text: Learned fugue in double counterpoint at the octave, tenth and twelfth

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times). Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted.

sections.label: Subject in G minor, rhythm varied (Tenor)
Episode 2
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times). Tenor: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and the opening of countersubject 1. Bass: free counterpoint, in a sequence rising by a fifth every bar.

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar. Bass: the opening of countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1.

sections.label: Together: Subject in B♭ major (Alto); Subject in B♭ major (Tenor)
Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted and a figure from countersubject 1. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted.

sections.label: Together: Subject in C minor, rhythm varied (Soprano); Subject in C minor (Alto)
Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted and the opening of countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every bar.

sections.label: Together: Subject in E♭ major, rhythm varied (Tenor); Subject in E♭ major (Bass)
Episode 6
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a third every beat. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a third every beat. Tenor: a figure from the subject and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a third every beat. Bass: a figure from the subject.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in G minor (Tenor); Subject in G minor (Soprano)
